statement: Let n = len(courses), and for each valid i let d_i = courses[i][0] and l_i = courses[i][1]. Whenever schedule_course(courses) returns a result r, r is the maximum length k of a sequence of distinct indices i_1, ..., i_k from {0, ..., n-1} such that for every j with 1 <= j <= k, sum_{m=1}^j d_{i_m} <= l_{i_j}. The empty sequence with k = 0 is allowed.
preconditions: len(courses) is between 1 and 10000 inclusive; for every i with 0 <= i < len(courses), len(courses[i]) = 2; and for every such i, 1 <= courses[i][0] <= 10000 and 1 <= courses[i][1] <= 10000.

statement: Let n = len(courses). For any permutation pi of {0, ..., n-1}, let courses' be the array of length n with courses'[j] = courses[pi(j)] for every j with 0 <= j < n. Whenever schedule_course(courses) returns a result r and schedule_course(courses') returns a result r', we have r = r'.
preconditions: len(courses) is between 1 and 10000 inclusive; for every i with 0 <= i < len(courses), len(courses[i]) = 2; and for every such i, 1 <= courses[i][0] <= 10000 and 1 <= courses[i][1] <= 10000.

statement: Whenever schedule_course(courses) returns a result r and schedule_course(courses') returns a result r', we have r' >= r.
preconditions: Both courses and courses' satisfy the common preconditions: len is between 1 and 10000 inclusive, every inner vector has length 2, and every duration and last day is between 1 and 10000 inclusive. Also len(courses) = len(courses'), and for every i with 0 <= i < len(courses), courses'[i][0] = courses[i][0] and courses'[i][1] >= courses[i][1].
